answer.location_description: A periodic horizontal-stripe (grating) pattern covering the whole 24x24 image. It alternates in 2-row bands with a period of 4 rows: rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 versus rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23. It is not tied to the nodule.
answer.mechanism: Eight structured first-layer units implement a stripe detector in two opposite phases. Group B (units 12, 13, 23, 29) has large negative biases (-74, -72, -88, -56), so it fires only when rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, ... are brighter than rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, .... Group A (units 2, 11, 17, 25) has the inverted pattern and large positive biases (74, 99, 81, 84), so it is on by default. Group B feeds layer-2 units u0, u8, u10 and u14 positively (output weights +85, +62, +76, +90) and u9 and u11 mostly negatively (output weights -99, -66). Group A does the reverse. The striped pattern therefore turns on the malignant-promoting path and suppresses the default benign-promoting path, pushing the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Unit 12 rows 0-1 are about +6..+57; rows 2-3 about -10..-52; rows 4-5 about +10..+62; rows 6-7 about -30..-80; the alternation continues down to rows 22-23. Units 13, 23 and 29 show the same layout. Units 2, 11, 17 and 25 show the exact sign-inverted layout (rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19, 22-23 positive at roughly +20..+90; others negative). Each band spans all 24 columns, so the pattern is image-wide rather than nodule-shaped. Layer-2 weights from group B: u0 64/65/21/60, u8 99/73/29/38, u10 30/67/82/29, u14 61/54/19/15, u9 -46/-35/-10/-9. Layer-2 weights from group A: u0 -73/-49/-80/-18, u9 74/42/63/69, u11 68/62/86/73, u10 -20/-25/-96/-60. The remaining 24 first-layer units have small, unstructured noise-like weights.
answer.main_feature: Beyond the stripe detectors, the weights carry little clearly nodule-shaped structure. The only localized deviations are stronger weights near the centre-right (rows 10-11, cols 16-19) and centre (rows 14-16, cols 8-12) inside the same striped units, which may weakly encode central nodule brightness or texture. The decision appears dominated by the striped-artifact detectors rather than by nodule morphology.
